messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: HIGH: GPU pool exhaustion detected in aws-us-west1 — autoscaler entering backoff, queue length > 600, customer impact reported. Pager runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-quota

maya: seeing a big spike in the inference queue, latency errors (503) reported from the hosted API. traffic pattern: steady then big tail since ~10m ago.

cj: oncall here. looking at autoscaler logs — get API to cloud returns 429 (quota) for new instance requests. scaling requests are being denied, so pods sit pending.

sasha: confirming — `kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving | grep Pending | wc -l` -> ~620 pending. NodePool shows desired=0->we're blocked on quota.

cj: customer impact: some enterprise customers seeing higher 5xx, a few complaints. throttling is broad; routing fallback didn't trigger for some pinned customers.

maya: quick mitigation idea: throttle non-critical batch jobs and reduce RPS for low-tier customers via rate-limiter config. can we toggle that from console?

devon: I can push a temporary rule to reduce the default token concurrency for non-enterprise to 2, rolling out now. will monitor. :fingers_crossed:

cj: doing on-call coordination: @sasha take infra lead, @devon apply rate-limits, i'll own cloud escalation and customer comms.

sasha: on it. first step: identify any idle GPUs in other regions we can failover to. running inventory query.

incident-bot: note: autoscaler backoff window = 15m, next attempt scheduled at +13m.

maya: another mitigation — can we promote a smaller model variant for a subset of traffic? e.g., rwd-small for non-SLAs to reduce GPU footprint.

sasha: we have canary config for smaller model. i can flip traffic for 20% of non-enterprise requests to rwd-small now. will do in 2min.

devon: rate-limit rule applied. non-enterprise concurrency reduced. seeing immediate drop in new queue growth rate.

cj: cloud support ticket opened: case #CS-987654. reported as quota/softlimit hit for GPUs in project redwood-prod in us-west-1. I've requested emergency quota bump and capacity guidance.

cloud-support: acknowledged. we've escalated to quota team. they report manual approval could take 30-90 minutes. temporary options: use alternate zone within region (requires image compatibility) or provision on-demand instances via partner account.

maya: list of critical customers (from ops list): acme, datawise-prod. devon — can you open targeted throttles for these customers? we need to ensure enterprise SLAs preserved.

devon: acme & datawise marked as high-priority; applying exception so they keep full capacity. throttling applied to everything else.

cj: sasha — status on failover to other regions?

sasha: inventory: us-west-2 has 120 spare GPUs, but latency penalty ~50ms. we can route failover for tolerant customers. i'll prepare routing change but need signoff from product for cross-region.

maya: product signoff via quick thread — ok to route non-SLA customers to us-west-2. enterprise traffic stays in us-west1 pinned.

cj: making a decision: route 40% of non-enterprise traffic to us-west-2, keep canary rwd-small for remaining. will document in incident timeline.

incident-bot: update: autoscaler still receiving 429 for new node requests. backoff extended.

devon: small-model canary flipped, rate-limits active, cross-region routing started for non-SLA. visible queue drop and 5xx rate falling from 4.2% -> 1.1% in last 5m.

cloud-support: quota team responded — there is a hard per-account regional allocation limit in us-west-1 that cannot be increased automatically. they offered workaround: clean up orphaned reserved capacity (we have 3 stale allocations) or open a business case for permanent increase (longer).

cj: action items: 1) sasha to reclaim stale reserved capacity (in progress), 2) devon keep throttles/canary, 3) maya coordinate customer comms for those impacted, 4) cj maintain cloud ticket and update execs.

maya: drafting customer message now — will post status page note: "Investigating increased error rates for inference in us-west-1; temporary mitigations in place. We are routing non-SLA traffic to alternative zones and limiting non-critical concurrency."

sasha: reclaimed 2 of 3 stale allocations -> freed 64 GPUs. autoscaler retried and 2 new nodes provisioned, some pending pods started.

cj: excellent — queue down to ~180. continuing to monitor. cs ticket updated (CS-987654) with reclamation details.

devon: leaving throttles in place for at least 30m after queue stabilizes. will gradually ramp if quotas remain stable.

cloud-support: quota team indicated the remaining hardcap requires account-level approval; timeline unclear. recommend long-term: spread reserved capacity across multiple projects to avoid single-account cap.

maya: post-incident: we'll need a runbook update for detecting stale reservations and an automated sweep to flag them. also add a routing policy to auto-fallback to other region for non-SLA within 5m.

cj: agreed. i'm handing off to morning oncall — @sasha continue monitoring and i’ll update the incident channel with postmortem plan.

sasha: taking over monitoring. will post summary in #incidents when stabilized.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations reduced customer impact. severity downgraded to MEDIUM. next update scheduled in 30m.
